chunks: Ahmad ibn Nasr ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us from Nahawand in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the year 29 AH (of the century), saying: Yahya ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad said to me: O Yahya ibn Abdullah,
He who spends a night without knowing his Imam will die a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).

key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً: A death of ignorance (pre-Islamic state of disbelief)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of not knowing the Imam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of the Minor and Major Ghebah, this hadith underscores the necessity of recognizing the living Imam to maintain valid religious authority. The term 'Jahiliyyah' here signifies a state of spiritual disconnection from divine guidance rather than mere historical ignorance, making Imamate the essential criterion for the acceptance of deeds. This concept is central to Shia jurisprudence, particularly in determining the validity of prayers and other acts of worship when the Imam is in occultation.
